subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Striking with Hands and Short Implements
title: Performance task build: striking with a short-handled paddle
essentialQuestion: How do I make solid, controlled contact with an object?
materials: unit equipment listed in the guardian safety review
movementCues: Shake-hands grip, thumb along the handle, wrist firm.
Hold the paddle out in front where you can see it and the object together.
Turn side-on to the direction you are striking.
Keep the swing short and controlled.
commonErrorToWatchFor: Gripping too tightly, which stiffens the swing. Fix: cue a grip firm enough to hold, loose enough to be taken from you.
keyPoints: Shake-hands grip, thumb along the handle, wrist firm.
Hold the paddle out in front where you can see it and the object together.
Turn side-on to the direction you are striking.
Keep the swing short and controlled.
privacySafeScenario: Sustain a cooperative rally with a partner or against a wall, and explain the contact point and follow-through that kept it going.
studentTask: The learner practises striking with a short-handled paddle at a self-selected challenge level, using the adapted alternative whenever it fits better, and names the cue that helped.
knowledgeCheck: The learner names one cue that helped with striking with a short-handled paddle and one adjustment for next time, by demonstrating, describing, drawing, or writing.
completionCriteria: The learner takes part in the task about striking with a short-handled paddle at a self-selected challenge level.
The learner uses or names the movement cues for striking with a short-handled paddle.
The learner identifies one adjustment or next step. No score, time, count, or measurement is required.
adaptationChoices: Striking may use a hand, a short paddle, or a long implement; a balloon, beach ball, or ball on a tee; and a shorter or seated swing. A learner may also call the contact point and follow-through for a partner instead of striking.
extensionChallenge: Apply striking with a short-handled paddle under one new condition of the learner choosing — different equipment, space, speed, or partner — and describe what changed.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show or describe a model before practice.
Allow demonstrated, described, drawn, spoken, signed, or written evidence; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-repetition, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-stimulation options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the movement target while adjusting equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, or support.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to enjoy one safe, optional activity that practises striking with a short-handled paddle. No purchase, account creation, recording, measurement, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
